```{r setup}
library(pkexport)
```
This vignette shows how to go from raw clinical PK tables to a file ready for Monolix, using the example data included in the package.

## Cleaning raw data with standardize_pk_data()

(Charlie's section)

## Exporting to Monolix with to_monolix()

Once the raw tables are combined into the standard table, `to_monolix()`
turns that table into a data file that Monolix can read. It does not change
any values. It only renames, recodes and reorders columns.

```{r monolix-std}
std <- standardize_pk_data(pk_doses, pk_levels, pk_covariates)
mlx <- to_monolix(std)
head(mlx, 8)
```

### How the columns are coded

| Monolix column | Comes from | Dose rows | Level rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| ID | ID | patient ID | patient ID |
| TIME | TIME | hours since first dose | hours since first dose |
| AMT | AMT | dose in mg | empty |
| TINF | DUR | infusion length in hours | empty |
| DV | CONC | empty | concentration in mg/L |
| EVID | EVENT | 1 | 0 |
| MDV | EVENT | 1 | 0 |
| AGE, SEX, WT_KG, SCR_MGDL | covariates | repeated on every row | repeated on every row |

EVENT and TAD are dropped, because Monolix works out the dosing history
itself from AMT, TINF and EVID. EVID = 1 marks a dose (an event that changes
the amount of drug), and MDV = 1 tells Monolix there is no observation on
that row.

The example data have the same number of rows before and after export, one
row per dose or level:

```{r monolix-check}
nrow(std)
nrow(mlx)
table(mlx$EVID)
```

### Writing the file

Give `to_monolix()` a file path to save the table as a .csv file. Empty cells
are written as `"."`, which Monolix reads as missing.

```{r monolix-file}
out_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
mlx <- to_monolix(std, file = out_file)
readLines(out_file, n = 5)
```

In Monolix, load this file as a new data set and assign the column types:
ID as **ID**, TIME as **TIME**, AMT as **AMOUNT**, TINF as **INFUSION DURATION**,
DV as **OBSERVATION**, EVID as **EVENT ID**, MDV as **MISSING DEPENDENT VARIABLE**,
WT_KG, AGE and SCR_MGDL as **CONTINUOUS COVARIATE**, and SEX as
**CATEGORICAL COVARIATE**.
